global_issues.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.1%, Stocks Slide on Rate Fears
global_issues.note: Confirmed by CNN/CNBC: 10Y yield hit 5.11%, highest since 2007 (19 years), driven by strong S&P Global PMI (58.4, 62-month high) and inflation concerns. S&P 500 -0.75-0.8%, Nasdaq -1.1%, Dow -0.7% on Sept 23. Fed Governor Barr reinforced hawkish tone same day, saying further hikes likely needed.

global_issues.title: Oil Falls to Two-Week Lows Near $89 Despite Iran Shipping Disruptions
global_issues.note: Reversed direction: WTI actually ROSE 1.8% on Sept 23 to $92.16, Brent +3.9% to $103.08, snapping a five-day LOSING streak (not falling to two-week lows near $89). Rally was driven by Iranian President Pezeshkian's defiant UN speech ('Iran cannot be made to surrender'), not eased by Trump-Iran talks. The briefing has the price level and the day's direction both wrong.

global_issues.title: Chip Export Bills Advance Amid Schumer Push and Xi Visit Looming
global_issues.note: Confirmed: Senate Democrats (Schumer) pushing trio of bills restricting AI chip exports to China, timed ahead of Trump-Xi summit (Wed/Thu Sept 23-24 at White House). Framing as 'looming' is slightly stale since the summit was starting the same day the briefing was generated, but substance is correct.

grok_report.summary: The Treasury yield and chip-export items check out and the market mood/sector framing is well-supported by same-day reporting, but the oil item is factually backwards — crude rose on Iran's defiant UN speech rather than falling to two-week lows, which is a real (not minor) error given oil's rank-2 placement.
